next_state_election.name: General Election
next_state_election.source_name: South Dakota Secretary of State — 2026 Election Information

glance_notes.source_name: South Dakota Secretary of State — Election FAQs
glance_notes.text: 2026 General Election Registration Deadline: South Dakota's voter registration deadline for the November 3, 2026 General Election is October 19 at 5:00 p.m. local time. The completed registration must be received by the county auditor by the deadline.

glance_notes.source_name: South Dakota Secretary of State — Absentee Voting
glance_notes.text: Absentee Voting Begins September 18: South Dakota allows registered voters to vote absentee without providing an excuse. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, absentee voting begins September 18. Registered voters may also vote absentee in person at their county auditor's office.

glance_notes.source_name: South Dakota Secretary of State — Register to Vote
glance_notes.text: 2026 Citizenship Documentation Rule: A South Dakota law effective March 26, 2026 requires a person newly registering to provide documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to become a full-ballot voter. A new registrant who does not provide the required citizenship documentation must be registered as a federal-only voter rather than being denied registration entirely.

register.label: Register to Vote
register.content: To register to vote in South Dakota, a person must be a U.S. citizen, be a South Dakota resident, be at least 18 years old by the next election, not currently be disqualified while serving a felony sentence under South Dakota law and not have been judged mentally incompetent by a court. South Dakota does not provide general online voter registration. Registration forms may be submitted to the appropriate county auditor through the methods permitted by state law. A new law effective March 26, 2026 requires new registrants to provide documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to become full-ballot voters. A new applicant who does not provide the required proof must be registered as a federal-only voter.
register.glance_value: Paper registration; new full-ballot registrants must document citizenship
register.source_name: South Dakota Secretary of State — Register to Vote
register.internal_note: IMPORTANT 2026 CHANGE: SB 175 took effect March 26, 2026. Under SDCL 12-4-1.4, a new voter who does not provide documentary proof of citizenship is registered as a federal-only voter. The Secretary of State lists acceptable citizenship evidence, including qualifying South Dakota or other state identification showing citizenship verification, tribal identification and specified citizenship documents. Existing registered voters are not accurately described as being universally required to re-prove citizenship. South Dakota's general voter-registration system is not online; the separate electronic UOCAVA portal is limited to qualifying military and overseas voters.

check_registration.label: Check Voter Registration
check_registration.content: Use South Dakota's Voter Information Portal to confirm your voter registration. The portal can also provide your polling place, sample ballot when available and absentee-ballot tracking information. A registration application is not final until it has been processed and accepted by the county election official. Voters who find incorrect information should contact their county auditor.
check_registration.glance_value: Check through the Voter Information Portal
check_registration.source_name: South Dakota Secretary of State — Voter Information Portal
check_registration.internal_note: The Secretary of State identifies the Voter Information Portal as the official tool for registration status, polling-place lookup, sample ballots and absentee-ballot tracking.

deadlines.label: Registration Deadlines
deadlines.content: South Dakota requires voter registration to be received by the county auditor no later than 5:00 p.m. local time 15 days before an election. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, the deadline is Monday, October 19 at 5:00 p.m. local time. A postmark by the deadline is not sufficient if the registration does not reach the county auditor in time. South Dakota does not provide general same-day voter registration.
deadlines.source_name: South Dakota Secretary of State — Election FAQs
deadlines.internal_note: The Secretary of State's current 2026 Election Information page identifies October 19 as the General Election registration deadline. The current Election FAQ specifies that the county auditor must receive registration by 5:00 p.m. 15 days before Election Day.

polling_place.label: Find a Polling Place
polling_place.content: Use South Dakota's Voter Information Portal to find the Election Day polling place assigned to your voter registration. Your polling place is also listed on the voter acknowledgement notice sent by the county election official after registration is accepted. Polling locations can change, so voters should confirm their assigned location before Election Day.
polling_place.glance_value: Find your polling place through the Voter Information Portal
polling_place.source_name: South Dakota Secretary of State — Voter Information Portal
polling_place.internal_note: The Secretary of State's General Voting Information page directly instructs voters to use the Voter Information Portal for polling-place information. The Secretary of State has also published 2026 precinct and polling-place information. Recheck voter-specific locations near Election Day.

election_day.label: Election Day Voting
election_day.content: South Dakota's General Election is Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Polling places are open from 7:00 a.m. until 7:00 p.m. local time. A voter who is in line when the polls close at 7:00 p.m. must be allowed to vote. Voters appearing at a polling place are asked to present an accepted photo ID. A voter who does not have an accepted photo ID may sign a personal identification affidavit and cast a regular ballot.
election_day.source_name: South Dakota Secretary of State — General Voting Information
election_day.internal_note: South Dakota's photo-ID rule has an important affidavit alternative. A voter lacking photo ID is not limited to a provisional ballot; the Secretary of State explicitly states that the voter may sign a personal identification affidavit and vote a regular ballot. Polling hours are 7:00 a.m.-7:00 p.m. local time, which matters because South Dakota spans two time zones.

polling_hours.label: Polling Hours
polling_hours.content: South Dakota polling places are open from 7:00 a.m. until 7:00 p.m. local time on Election Day. Anyone who is already in line when the polls close at 7:00 p.m. is entitled to vote.
polling_hours.source_name: South Dakota Secretary of State — General Voting Information
polling_hours.internal_note: The phrase local time should remain in the reader-facing record because South Dakota includes both Central and Mountain Time areas. The current Secretary of State FAQ confirms that anyone in line by 7:00 p.m. is entitled to vote.

early_voting.label: Early In-Person Absentee Voting
early_voting.content: South Dakota does not use a separate traditional early-voting system. Instead, any registered voter may vote absentee in person without an excuse once absentee voting begins. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, absentee voting begins Friday, September 18. Registered voters may go to their county auditor's office during available office hours, present an accepted photo ID and cast an absentee ballot. A voter without photo ID may sign a personal identification affidavit and vote a regular absentee ballot. Some jurisdictions may also provide authorized absentee satellite locations.
early_voting.source_name: South Dakota Secretary of State — Absentee Voting
early_voting.internal_note: The official 2026 Election Information page establishes September 18 as the beginning of General Election absentee voting. South Dakota's functional early-voting option is in-person absentee voting. The Secretary of State has also published 2026 General Election satellite-site information. County-specific and satellite hours should be rechecked before Election Day rather than presenting a uniform statewide daily schedule.

absentee_mail.label: Absentee Voting
absentee_mail.content: Any registered South Dakota voter may vote absentee without providing an excuse. A voter requesting an absentee ballot by mail must submit an absentee-ballot application to the county election official. The application generally must include a photocopy of an acceptable photo ID or be notarized, although different rules apply to qualifying military and overseas voters. A voter may also apply for an absentee ballot in person at the county auditor's office during regular office hours through 5:00 p.m. on the day before the election. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, absentee voting begins September 18. A completed absentee ballot must reach the county election official in enough time to be delivered to the voter's polling place before the polls close at 7:00 p.m. local time on Election Day.
absentee_mail.glance_value: No excuse; absentee voting begins September 18
absentee_mail.source_name: South Dakota Secretary of State — Absentee Voting
absentee_mail.internal_note: South Dakota permits no-excuse absentee voting. The ordinary absentee application requires either qualifying identification documentation or notarization. UOCAVA voters receive an exemption from that requirement. The Secretary of State states that completed absentee ballots must be received in time to be delivered to the polling place before polls close. Current FAQ guidance summarizes the practical deadline as receipt by the county auditor by 7:00 p.m. Election Day.

voter_id.label: Voter ID Requirements
voter_id.content: South Dakota asks voters appearing at a polling place to show an accepted photo ID. Accepted identification includes a South Dakota driver's license or nondriver identification card, a U.S. government photo ID such as a passport, a U.S. Armed Forces identification card, a current student photo identification card issued by a South Dakota high school or accredited South Dakota institution of higher education, or a tribal photo identification card. A voter who does not have an accepted photo ID may sign a personal identification affidavit and is still allowed to cast a regular ballot.
voter_id.glance_value: Photo ID requested; affidavit allows a regular ballot without ID
voter_id.source_name: South Dakota Secretary of State — General Voting Information
voter_id.internal_note: Do not describe South Dakota as an absolute photo-ID state or say a voter without ID must cast a provisional ballot. SDCL 12-18-6.1 and current Secretary of State guidance allow a voter without photo identification to sign a personal identification affidavit and cast a regular ballot. South Dakota student IDs qualify only when issued by a South Dakota high school or accredited South Dakota institution of higher education.

accessible_voting.label: Accessible Voting
accessible_voting.content: South Dakota provides accessible polling places and voting equipment for voters with disabilities. Voters with disabilities or physical limitations may ask for assistance at the polling place and may contact their county election official before Election Day if special arrangements are needed. For federal elections, every polling place must provide a voting device that allows voters with disabilities to vote privately and independently. South Dakota uses the ExpressVote ballot-marking system, which provides features including enlarged text, reverse contrast, audio instructions, a keypad and compatibility with certain assistive input devices. Absentee voting is also available without an excuse.
accessible_voting.glance_value: Accessible polling places, ExpressVote and voting assistance
accessible_voting.source_name: South Dakota Secretary of State — Polling Place Accessibility
accessible_voting.internal_note: The ExpressVote is a paper-based electronic ballot-marking device. It does not tabulate votes or retain voter selections. The voter receives a paper ballot activator card, uses the device to mark selections and then casts the resulting paper ballot. Current Secretary of State guidance confirms accessible equipment at federal-election polling places and assistance for voters with disabilities or physical limitations.

military_overseas.label: Military & Overseas Voting
military_overseas.content: South Dakota provides special registration and absentee-voting procedures for eligible uniformed-service members, qualifying spouses and dependents, and U.S. citizens living overseas. Covered voters may use the Federal Post Card Application to register and request an absentee ballot. South Dakota also operates a UOCAVA electronic portal for qualifying voters who have a current valid South Dakota driver's license or nondriver identification card. UOCAVA voters may submit signed absentee-ballot applications by mail, fax or scanned email and may request electronic delivery of their ballot. A voted official ballot cannot be returned electronically; it must be printed and returned by mail. The completed ballot must arrive in time to be delivered to the appropriate polling location before the polls close on Election Day.
military_overseas.glance_value: Electronic application and ballot delivery; voted ballot returned physically
military_overseas.source_name: South Dakota Secretary of State — Military Members
military_overseas.internal_note: Current Secretary of State UOCAVA guidance is explicit that electronic ballot DELIVERY is available but a MARKED official ballot may not be returned electronically by email or fax. The voter must print and physically return the ballot. UOCAVA absentee applications may be submitted electronically, and the ordinary photo-ID/notarization requirement for absentee applications is waived for qualifying military and overseas voters. The FWAB is available when applicable.

student_voting.label: College / Student Voting
student_voting.content: College students may choose where to establish their South Dakota voting residence. A South Dakota resident who moves to another county to attend college may register at the student's current on-campus or off-campus address or remain registered at the student's prior South Dakota home address. A student from another state may choose to establish South Dakota voting residence and register in South Dakota if eligible, or may continue voting under the absentee rules of the student's home state. A voter may be registered and vote in only one place at a time. A current student photo ID from a South Dakota high school or accredited South Dakota institution of higher education is an accepted form of identification for in-person voting.
student_voting.glance_value: Students may choose a qualifying school or home residence
student_voting.source_name: South Dakota Secretary of State — College Students
student_voting.internal_note: The Secretary of State directly gives South Dakota college students the choice between their current college residence and prior South Dakota home address. Students from other states may register in South Dakota if they establish eligibility or vote absentee through their home state. Current South Dakota high school and accredited higher-education student photo IDs are specifically accepted for voting.

sample_ballot.label: Official Sample Ballot
sample_ballot.content: Registered South Dakota voters can use the Voter Information Portal to view their sample ballot when it is available. The portal also provides voter registration information, polling-place information and absentee-ballot tracking. Because ballot contents depend on the voter's residence and districts, voters should use their own voter record to retrieve the ballot that applies to them for the November 3, 2026 General Election.
sample_ballot.glance_value: View your sample ballot in the Voter Information Portal
sample_ballot.source_name: South Dakota Secretary of State — Voter Information Portal
sample_ballot.internal_note: The Secretary of State's Elections and Voting page explicitly identifies View Sample Ballot as a Voter Information Portal function. Reverify after final 2026 General Election ballots are available because voter-specific contests vary by district.

contact.label: Contact the State Election Authority
contact.content: South Dakota Secretary of State, Elections Division, 500 East Capitol Avenue, Suite 204, Pierre, SD 57501. Phone: 605-773-3537. Toll-free HAVA assistance: 888-703-5328. Fax: 605-773-6580. Email: Elections@state.sd.us. For voter-specific registration, polling-place or absentee-ballot questions, voters should also contact their county auditor.
contact.source_name: South Dakota Secretary of State — Elections Division
contact.internal_note: Current Secretary of State election materials verify 500 East Capitol Avenue, Suite 204, Pierre, SD 57501; 605-773-3537; fax 605-773-6580; and [Elections@state.sd.us](mailto:Elections@state.sd.us). Current HAVA materials also list toll-free 888-703-5328. The email address is intentionally plain text with no Markdown or mailto wrapper.

official_resources.label: Official State & Local Resources
official_resources.content: Use the South Dakota Secretary of State Elections Division and Voter Information Portal for official election information. These resources provide voter registration requirements, registration status, polling places, sample ballots, absentee voting, absentee-ballot tracking, voter identification requirements, accessible voting information, military and overseas voting resources and county election official contacts. County auditors administer voter registration, absentee voting and many local election functions.
